name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+9 and the national environment favors Democrats
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but not the partisan baseline
Irwin holds a large cash and outside-spending edge over Gallucci
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean plus a favorable environment give Democrats a large built-in edge even with Julia Brownley retiring, and Jacqui Irwin's fundraising, cash position, and outside backing far exceed Sam Gallucci's thin war chest. Prediction markets price the seat as all but decided for Democrats.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing a much tighter race or a late wave of Republican outside spending would be the clearest sign to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District leans Democratic by nine points, and Julia Brownley's retirement turns this into an open-seat contest rather than a straightforward incumbent race. Democrat Jacqui Irwin holds a clear financial edge, with about $822,000 raised, nearly $296,000 in cash on hand, and more than $366,000 in outside support. Republican Sam Gallucci has raised roughly $489,000 but reports under $29,000 remaining, with no recorded outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so fundamentals and markets carry the forecast. The district's Democratic lean, a favorable national environment, and a wide money gap point to a comfortable Democratic margin. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent. The main uncertainty is the absence of direct polling in an open-seat year, where turnout patterns can shift results.
